diagnosis.summary: The nightly run 1c1f4ada for 2026-10-01 failed at quality_checks because the upstream payments file for that day contains every payment twice. There are 834 rows but only 417 unique payment_ids, and the two copies are identical. Following the duplicates runbook (Cause A), I proposed deduplicating payments on payment_id at ingest. It isn't applied yet: the harness will apply it and rerun the pipeline. Upstream should still be told about the doubled export.

root_cause.explanation: The 2026-10-01 payments landing file has 834 rows. Every one of its 417 payment_ids appears exactly twice, with identical order_id, method, amount and paid_ts. The ids don't overlap with the 2026-09-30 file and all timestamps fall on the partition day (one is a few minutes past midnight), so these are not stale rows resent from an earlier day. The ingest config has no dedupe key, so raw.payments kept both copies. That made unique_stg_payments_payment_id, assert_payments_match_orders and row_count_trend fail, and the fct_orders tests were skipped. fct_orders also has 0 rows for 2026-10-01, which is why the freshness and reconciliation checks fail. I didn't confirm why it is empty. My best guess is that the build was blocked by the payments failures.

evidence.claim: Run 1c1f4ada failed at quality_checks; ingest and transform succeeded
raw.payments has 834 rows, 190% of the trailing median of 439; the unique payment_id test and the payments-match-orders test each found 417 failing rows
All 417 payment_ids appear exactly twice as identical full rows in the 2026-10-01 file. They aren't stale rows from 2026-09-30, and the schema matches the contract.
fct_orders has 0 rows for 2026-10-01 against 440 raw orders, and its tests were skipped
No dbt models changed and the ingest config has no dedupe key
For identical copies inside one file, the runbook says to use deduplicate_on_ingest on the table's primary key

alternatives_considered: stale_rows_resent: ruled out because the payment_ids don't overlap with 2026-09-30 and all timestamps fall on the partition day
bad_model_deploy and revert_model_change: ruled out because no dbt models changed
request_upstream_redelivery: the runbook allows it, but deduping is the recommended fix for identical copies inside one file and doesn't depend on upstream
schema change and column mapping: ruled out because the header matches the contract

proposal.rationale: The 2026-10-01 payments landing file has every one of 417 payment_ids exactly twice, as identical full-row copies. The ids don't overlap with 2026-09-30, all timestamps are on the partition day, and the schema matches the contract. This is runbook Cause A (duplicates inside one file), and the runbook remedy is deduplicate_on_ingest on the primary key payment_id. Deduping restores 417 unique payments, which is normal volume. That clears the unique_stg_payments_payment_id, assert_payments_match_orders and row_count_trend failures and unblocks the fct_orders build and its tests. No dbt models changed, so a model revert doesn't apply.

applied: ingest now keeps one row per payment_id when loading raw.payments
